Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
938 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) One more round of coastal flooding is expected with this 
morning's high tide cycle with many locations likely seeing 
minor flood benchmarks reached. Beach flooding and dune erosion 
expected to continue through at least this morning and 
potentially into the afternoon.

2) Rainfall anticipated today and Sunday night into early Monday 
morning. No adverse impacts anticipated.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Locations most likely to see minor flooding will be around the 
NY Harbor and the South Shore LI Bays. There is less confidence 
in minor flooding along the LI Sound. Additionally, this 
generally looks like a more low end minor threat. Low confidence
in reaching locally moderate. If this were to happen, the most 
reasonable location would be southern Nassau. Given some 
uncertainty, have left the Coastal Flood Advisory in effect for 
all locations.

Beach flooding and dune erosion will continue through at least this 
morning with the swell direction becoming briefly perpendicular to 
the coast. Breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet continue this morning and 
gradually diminish through the day with ocean seas diminishing and 
the direction becoming more SW.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
500mb low and attendant surface low pass to our NW through northern 
NY today. Embedded shortwaves aloft and upward forcing with the 
proximity of the surface low combined with residual moisture will 
bring light rainfall and showers to the area today with the highest 
overall chances NW of the city. SW winds gust 20-30 mph today.

Rain is then expected Sunday night into early Monday with low 
pressure tracking NW form the eastern Great Lakes to Northern New 
England. Some models also depict a secondary low or triple point 
potentially moving through the forecast area during this period. 
Expecting rainfall, with the highest probability of occurrence 
during the late night hours of Sunday night. Probably looking at 
about a half inch of rainfall, so no hydrologic impacts anticipated. 
A low level jet associated with the secondary low/triple point may 
help contribute to gusty winds as well as a slight chance of thunder 
with some elevated instability noted in some guidance. Right now any 
wind impacts would appear to be minimal.

&&

.AVIATION /15Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
The terminals will remain between departing low pressure and 
high pressure to the south through Saturday.

Mainly MVFR although there will be periods of VFR, especially
the remainder of this morning and then the potential of another
period of VFR tonight. There is also a chance for a few showers
this afternoon/early evening. Brief MVFR vsby is possible in 
these showers.

Winds generally SW at 10-15 kt with gusts of 20-25 kt through 
the period.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
Ceilings may fluctuate between MVFR and VFR through the TAF
period. Ceiling heights in MVFR should remain 020-030. 

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z Saturday through Tuesday... 

Saturday: MVFR ceilings. W winds G20-25kt, diminishing at 
night.

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night: Showers likely with MVFR cond. or lower after 
midnight.

Monday: Chance of morning showers with MVFR cond. SW winds G20-25kt, 
becoming W in the afternoon and NW at night.

Tuesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Gale Warnings in effect through tonight on the ocean waters with SCA 
on the non ocean waters for the same time period. SCA conds likely 
follow on the ocean for Saturday, and possibly for the non ocean 
waters as well. While the forecast on the non ocean waters 
advertises gusts to 25kt during Saturday, have decided to wait on 
extending the SCA here into Saturday as it's in the 3rd period and 
it's also possible that pressure gradient over the area trends 
weaker. Ocean seas today remain quite elevated due to residual 
swell, which should impact the entrances of LI Sound and NY Harbor 
for much of the day. Outside of residual swell on the ocean during 
the morning, sub-advisory conditions are expected on all waters for 
Sunday. Winds and seas then ramp up Sunday night into Monday with 
the approach and passage of a low pressure system. Gales on the 
ocean waters are anticipated, and possibly some non-ocean zones 
could see a few gale force gusts. Will include mention of this for 
the ocean waters in the HWO for the time being.
